pr_body:
This PR adds support for multiple package registries.

Currently implemented are 
- [Composer](https://getcomposer.org/)
- [Conan](https://conan.io/)
- Container ([Docker](https://www.docker.com/) / [Helm](https://helm.sh/))
- Generic packages
- [Maven](https://maven.apache.org)
- [npm](https://www.npmjs.com/)
- [NuGet](https://www.nuget.org/)
- [PyPI](https://pypi.org/)
- [RubyGems](https://guides.rubygems.org/)

Every user/org has an own package registry for all different types of packages.

> publish npm package seems return failure.

That's a strange behaviour. If `author` is set in your `project.json` the request contains a `"author":{"name":"..."}` object. But if `author` is not set the request contains `"author":""`. In the first case it's an object and in the second a string. Now the json parser is complaining.

One thing, however - Does this handle the generation of maven-metadata.xml files?  I use Renovate on my Gitea instance and I currently have a Sonatype Nexus 3 OSS deployed with the Maven repository.  Renovate refused to work until the maven-metadata.xml files were generated.

> > > add a download counter like npmjs.com have it.
> > 
> > 
> > I don't know if we want that feature. And if we do, how fine grained it should be. For example a simple download counter or "today", "week", ... As there are package types with multiple files I don't know at the moment how to count the downloads. If every file download adds one, for two files the package download counter would increase by two.
> 
> I think all package managers only have one endpoint which can be used to count a package as a Download + 1. For the generic package you could use the sum of all files. And for the visualization you could also take a look at githubs kind of chart. I think this also looks pretty good.

Yes, there is only one endpoint but it gets called multiple times for a single package download. For example Maven: 2-3 hits (x.jar, x.pom, maven-metadata.xml), Python (x.whl, x.tar.gz). In these cases a simple +1 does not work.

> > > why does the generic package dont show the README.md and dont allow to upload multiple assets?
> > 
> > 
> > Readme support is not planned. Multiple assets may be allowed. This may be a problem for a potential download counter.
> 
> Why is that not the planed? A npm package also shows me a readme.

Most packages contain metadata. The npm package manager embeds the whole readme file into the metadata. This is displayed on the detail page, not the readme file contained in the package itself.

> > > show also the package.jsons keywords in the sidebar
> > 
> > 
> > done for npm
> 
> Does such a information also exists on other package managers?

Nuget can have `tags` in the package metadata.

> > > allow to download packages without authentication
> > 
> > 
> > done
> 
> Is this for all packages, or is there an option for the repo owner?

For all packages. If anonymous access it not allowed for a repository it is not allowed for packages too.

> 2. What is with docker packages?

I have a (unpublished) PR which adds support for containers. It passes all OCI conformance tests and therefore works with every OCI client, docker included. But because the data structure does not match with the "normal" packages I will not add it into this PR. It's large enough 😉

> One thing, however - Does this handle the generation of maven-metadata.xml files? I use Renovate on my Gitea instance and I currently have a Sonatype Nexus 3 OSS deployed with the Maven repository. Renovate refused to work until the maven-metadata.xml files were generated.

The "what versions are available" `maven-metadata.xml` gets generated on the fly. The snapshot `maven-metadata.xml` is just the provided one by maven when publishing a package.

Sounds like scope creep to me. I appreciate the narrow scope and purpose of Gitea and wouldn't want this merged. If someone wants a package registry, there are standalone solutions that can be implemented.

> Sounds like scope creep to me. I appreciate the narrow scope and purpose of Gitea and wouldn't want this merged. If someone wants a package registry, there are standalone solutions that can be implemented.

Providing built source code is not that far outside the scope of a source code management system...

You said it yourself, it's a source code management system. This isn't source code. Gitea shouldn't be managing it. There's not even a built in CI system for Gitea to build the packages.

If there were a precedent set for Gitea including devops features, like a CI system, this would make sense. But it's not making sense to me with what Gitea is currently.

I talked with @lunny the last days about the package registry "scope". Currently every repository has its own independent registry. The alternative would be a user/org registry. I have listed some pro/cons we should consider to make a decision. Note: GitHub supports only user/org registries (with packages associated to a repository) while GitLab uses repository registries. GitLab allows to use an user/org endpoint for some package types. ### GitHub For GitHub every package (except containers) must be associated with a repository. Because only an user/org endpoint is available, the reference for a repository must be set in the package metadata (npm: `"repository": "https://github.com/user/repo"`). If you try to push a second image with the same name but a reference to another repository, you get an error message like `Package xxx is already associated with another repository`. ### GitLab For GitLab every package is associated with a repository because the repository is the registry. Because of this you do not have to specify a repository reference in the package metadata. This allows to push third-party packages to the registry where you can't control the metadata. You can push the same package to multiple repository-registries without problems because they are independent. This leads to problems with user/org endpoints because there are now multiple packages with the same name (and maybe different versions). Note 2: The need for the repository-association is the inherited permission model of the repository. If a user has access to the repository, he has access to the packages. For GitHub container-packages not associated with a repository, you can choose if the visibility is public or private. | | GitHub | GitLab | | - | - | - | | Pro | - Every package is available from one endpoint
- No name collissions | - Repository reference not needed | | Contra | - Repository reference in package metadata needed | - Name collissions with user/org endpoints
- Duplicated endpoints (user/org scope, registry scope) | Currently implemented is the GitLab version without the user/org endpoints, so there are no name collissions. The downside is you may have to specify multiple package registries in a project because the dependency packages may be spread over multiple repositories (the alternative would be a single repository which contains all packages). For Gitea we may not enforce the association to a repository when publishing a package to the user/org endpoint. In this case we could allow to manually set a repository reference later in the UI (GitHub allows this for unassociated containers). Because a repository reference is missing, there is no permission model. Maybe all these packages should be private for the user/org then. This would get us all pros and may prevent to contras. An edge case would be a manually associated package for which you publish a new version without repository reference. Would that package be automatically associated with the repository of the present package version?

I think the GitLab model is better. The Pro of GitHub model (Con of GitLab model) can not be a problem:

1. The endpoint problem: users can setup a separate repository for package purpose.
2. The name collision problem: as 1, a special package repository also works.

To help testing I created a list with steps how to create and publish a minimal package of every type.

{username} = your username
{password} = your password
{token} = your personal access token

The examples use the default `http://localhost:3000/` url.

## Composer

```shell
composer init

zip -r php-package.zip .

curl --user {username}:{password} --upload-file php-package.zip http://localhost:3000/api/packages/{username}/composer?version=1.0.3
```

## Conan

```shell
conan remote add gitea http://localhost:3000/api/packages/{username}/conan

conan user --remote gitea -p {password} {username}

# optional: conan config set general.revisions_enabled=1

conan new ConanPackage/1.2 -t

conan create . test/final

conan upload --remote=gitea ConanPackage/1.2@test/final --all
```

## Container

```shell
# pull a random image
docker pull {image}:latest

docker tag {image}:latest localhost:3000/{username}/{image}:latest

# you may need --insecure for http access (or edit your docker config)
docker login localhost:3000

docker push localhost:3000/{username}/{image}:latest
```

## Generic

```shell
curl --user {username}:{password} --upload-file file.bin http://localhost:3000/api/packages/{username}/generic/generic-package/1.0.3/file.bin

curl --user {username}:{password} http://localhost:3000/api/packages/{username}/generic/generic-package/1.0.3/file.bin
```

```shell
mvn archetype:generate -DgroupId=io.gitea -DartifactId=maven-package -DarchetypeArtifactId=maven-archetype-quickstart

nano ~/.m2/settings.xml
```
```xml
<settings>

    <server>
      <id>gitea</id>
      <configuration>
        <httpHeaders>
          <property>
            <name>Authorization</name>
            <value>token {token}</value>
          </property>
        </httpHeaders>
      </configuration>
    </server>
  </servers>
</settings>
```
```shell
cd maven-package

nano pom.xml
```
```xml
<project ...>
  ...
  <repositories>
    <repository>
      <id>gitea</id>
      <url>http://localhost:3000/api/packages/{owner}/maven</url>

  </repositories>
```

You may encounter errors like `Source option 5 is no longer supported. Use 6 or later.` or `Target option 1.5 is no longer supported. Use 1.6 or later.`. This can be fixed with an addition to the `pom.xml`:

issue_context.title: Github owns NPM now with future integrations to come - what would Gitea NPM (PHP/Python/etc) support look like?
issue_context.body:
This is more of a discussion than a feature request.

In terms of supporting NPM repos, it looks like Github and NPM could potentially merge.  Github has announced better integrations between their platform and NPM.

For me it's a no brainer and could allow Gitea to support other repository types (python, go, PHP, node) if it was provided as a plugin or architecture which allows it.  They are all similar in terms of what they do - build, tag, host, publishing.

Do we want Gitea to have this?

To support an NPM (or other repository types)  what would be needed?
comments: There is already work in this direction #14919
